newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bosnia war criminals threaten peace - U.S. General.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia war criminals threaten peace - U.S. General.

text.p: The United States' top soldier said on Wednesday the liberty of indicted war criminals in Bosnia was a persistent threat to peace in the region.

"For the Dayton Agreement to have a good chance, the international community will have to come to grips with the necessity of bringing war criminals to justice in The Hague," General John Shalikashvili told reporters.
Asked if he thought those indicted should be brought to the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague before that deadline, he said: "Yes I would think so."
Shalikashvili promised to "make every day count" before the planned withdrawal of U.S. troops from Bosnia next year.
He reiterated that U.S. troops would withdraw from Bosnia in June 1998 but said pressure would be applied in the meantime to ensure compliance from all parties with the Dayton peace plan.
"If we do our tasks correctly the situation we will face in June will be very different. We must make every day count from now until June," he said.
Shalikashvili was speaking to reporters after talks in the Netherlands with senior Dutch military officials.
The U.N. war crimes tribunal has indicted over 70 people since it was set up by the Security Council in 1993 but it currently has only nine of them in its custody.
Indicted war crimes suspects still at large include former Bosnian Serb leaders Radovan Karadzic and General Ratko Mladic, both of whom have been charged with genocide.
